newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends near limit down on soybean losses.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends near limit down on soybean losses.

text.p: CBOT corn futures posted near limit losses at the close on Wednesday, pressured by a collapse in soybeans and reports China was poised to sell more corn, traders said.
Soybeans fell sharply amid news Brazil had sold 45,000 tonnes of soybeans to a U.S. firm.
"Corn was a follower," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International. "Brazil is on stream now, not just to Europe and the Pacific Rim but to us, too."
Nearby corn tumbled the 12-cent daily limit minutes before the close but recovered to end just off limit losses.

Traders cited reports that Far East grain traders expect Chinese exports to increase, possibly even double this year. A trader in Seoul said China's corn sales to South Korea alone since the start of 1997 were 690,500 tonnes and could hit 1.5 million tonnes for the year.
That scenario prompted speculation USDA may eventually need to cut U.S. export estimates and increase 1996-97 ending stocks projections from 959 million bushels.
Corn closed 11-1/4 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower with May off 11-1/4 at $2.94-1/2 a bushel and December off seven at $2.80-3/4.
Still, Taiwan bought 108,000 tonnes of U.S. corn overnight and bulls maintained China would be only a temporary player in a world market the United States still dominated.

Commercials were buyers under the market with most major cash-connected houses said to be on the buy-side. Cargill Inc reportedly bought five million bushels May and 1.5 million July, ADM bought three million May, two million March and one million each July and December.
Term Commodities bought five million May, Continental Grain bought two million May and FCC bought three million May, traders said.
Funds began to liquidate positions they had built up for the last two months. Traders said the market had been braced for fund liquidation since fund buying pushed nearbys over the $3 mark.
Refco Inc sold three million bushels May, Griffin Trading sold 3.5 million May and Dean Witter sold at least one million May, traders said.
In options trade, Tenco bought 1,000 May $2.70 puts at one cent, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 500 July $3.50 calls and 5-1/4 and Griffin Trading bought 500 May $3.00 puts at eight to 8-1/2 cents.
